questions.question: In Preamble & Citizenship, this exam clue belongs to which area: "WE, THE PEOPLE OF INDIA, having solemnly resolved to constitute India into a SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC and to secure to all its citizens..."?
questions.explanation: Preamble — The Text: WE, THE PEOPLE OF INDIA, having solemnly resolved to constitute India into a SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC and to secure to all its citizens: JUSTICE(social, economic, political), LIBERTY(thought, expression, belief, faith, worship), EQUALITY(status, opportunity), FRATERNITY(dignity of individual+unity and integrity of nation). Words Socialist+Secular+Integrity: added by 42nd Amendment(1976, during Emergency). Original Preamble had only Sovereign+Democratic+Republic.

questions.question: In Preamble & Citizenship, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Berubari Union Case(1960): SC held Preamble is NOT part of the Constitution — cannot be used to interpret Articles. Kesavananda Bharati Case(1973): SC REVERSED Berubari..."?
questions.explanation: Preamble — Key Legal Cases: Berubari Union Case(1960): SC held Preamble is NOT part of the Constitution — cannot be used to interpret Articles. Kesavananda Bharati Case(1973): SC REVERSED Berubari — held Preamble IS part of the Constitution and can be used to interpret provisions. But Preamble is still NOT justiciable(cannot be enforced as a legal right in court). LIC of India Case(1995): Reaffirmed Preamble IS part of the Constitution.

questions.question: In Preamble & Citizenship, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Source of authority: WE THE PEOPLE : Popular Sovereignty. Nature of State : Sovereign(no external authority above India)+Socialist(social+economic equality, added..."?
questions.explanation: What the Preamble Declares: Source of authority: WE THE PEOPLE : Popular Sovereignty. Nature of State : Sovereign(no external authority above India)+Socialist(social+economic equality, added 1976)+Secular(state has no official religion, all religions equal, added 1976)+Democratic(elected government)+Republic(elected head of state, no hereditary monarchy). Objectives : Justice+Liberty+Equality+Fraternity. Date : 26th November 1949.

questions.question: In Preamble & Citizenship, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Part II of Constitution. Art 5: Citizenship at commencement(born in India+parents born in India OR 5yrs ordinary residence). Art 6: Citizenship of migrants from Pakistan..."?
questions.explanation: Citizenship — Art 5–11 + Citizenship Act 1955: Part II of Constitution. Art 5: Citizenship at commencement(born in India+parents born in India OR 5yrs ordinary residence). Art 6: Citizenship of migrants from Pakistan. Art 7: Citizenship of migrants to Pakistan. Art 8: Citizens of Indian origin outside India. Art 9: Voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship : loss of Indian citizenship. Art 10: Continuance of citizenship. Art 11: Parliament can make laws on citizenship. Citizenship Act 1955: By birth(before 1987: jus soli, 1987-2003: one parent Indian, after 2003: neither parent foreign national), By descent, By registration, By naturalization(11 years residence).

questions.question: In Preamble & Citizenship, this exam clue belongs to which area: "CAA 2019: Fast-tracks citizenship for persecuted Hindu+Sikh+Buddhist+Jain+Parsi+Christian minorities from Pakistan+Bangladesh+Afghanistan who entered India before Dec 31..."?
questions.explanation: Citizenship Amendment Act 2019: CAA 2019: Fast-tracks citizenship for persecuted Hindu+Sikh+Buddhist+Jain+Parsi+Christian minorities from Pakistan+Bangladesh+Afghanistan who entered India before Dec 31, 2014. Reduction of residence requirement : 11 years→5 years for these communities. Muslims NOT included: controversy. Does NOT apply to tribal areas of NE(6th Schedule states) and states with Inner Line Permit(Arunachal, Nagaland, Mizoram, Manipur). NRC(National Register of Citizens) linked concern but officially separate.

lesson_intro: With the Constitution's skeleton (Day 1) and its Schedules (Day 2) locked in your memory, today you study the two most philosophically important opening sections: the Preamble and Citizenship. The Preamble is often called the soul of the Constitution — it declares the fundamental purposes and values that the entire document is built on. It is also the subject of one of the most dramatic legal reversals in Indian constitutional history: the Supreme Court first said the Preamble was NOT part of the Constitution (Berubari Union case, 1960), then completely reversed itself and said it IS (Kesavananda Bharati case, 1973). Citizenship, covered in Part II (Articles 5–11), defines who belongs to India and on what terms — a question that became politically explosive again with the Citizenship Amendment Act 2019.

quick_note_cards.back: Berubari Union (1960): Preamble is NOT part of Constitution. Cannot be used for interpretation. Kesavananda Bharati (1973): REVERSED — Preamble IS part of Constitution. CAN be used for interpretation. But STILL not justiciable (cannot be enforced in court as a right).

quick_note_cards.title: Exam Card

quick_note_cards.back: Socialist + Secular + Integrity. Added in 1976 during Emergency (Indira Gandhi government). Original Preamble(1949) had: Sovereign, Democratic, Republic only. Note: FRATERNITY was original — not added later.
quick_note_cards.front: Which 3 words were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment?
quick_note_cards.title: Exam Card

quick_note_cards.back: Popular Sovereignty — the people of India are the ultimate source of authority. The Constitution derives its authority from the people, not from Parliament or any government. Parliament derives its power FROM the Constitution, not the other way around.
quick_note_cards.front: What does "We the People" in the Preamble signify?
quick_note_cards.title: Exam Card

quick_note_cards.back: Before 1987: Born in India : Indian citizen (Jus Soli — place of birth). 1987-2003: Born in India + at least one parent Indian citizen. After 2003: Born in India + neither parent a foreign national + neither parent illegal migrant. Rules became progressively stricter.
quick_note_cards.front: Citizenship at birth — how did the rules change?
